items.text: Your own files whose names only look like temporary files are no longer ignored. items.text: **Changed:** a page file named by a date, such as `pages/2026-11-02.md` or a page whose `title::` is a date, is now that day's journal instead of an ordinary page named `2026-11-02`. It stays where it is: Tine does not move, merge or rewrite it on its own, and your edits of the day are saved into that file. `[[Nov 2nd, 2026]]`, `[[2026-11-02]]`, the Journals feed and opening the day all use it, and its linked references are the day's. When both `journals/2026_11_02.md` and `pages/2026-11-02.md` exist, the journals one is shown, and while both exist the other file's aliases and links count for nothing; Tine merges or rewrites neither on its own. A day with no file still gets a new one in `journals/`. More generally, when a file in `journals/` and a file in `pages/` have the same name, the one in `journals/` now comes first and opens. With a journal title format without a year (such as `MM-dd`), a page named like `11-02` stays an ordinary page, the same date in two years stays two days, and a day is found by its date, not by that shared label (REG-CM-S2-DAY-FILE, REG-CM-S2-DAY-ORDER, REG-CM-S2-YEARLESS-LABEL, REG-CM-S2-YEARLESS-RETITLE, REG-CM-S2-DAY-FILE-CONFLICT-KIND).

items.text: **Changed:** a rename checks every name it touches, not only the page itself: each name under the page (from a file, a link, or any page's alias) and the page's own aliases. If one of them would become a name another page already holds, or several files claim one, the rename is refused and says which name and which page or files, instead of silently folding pages together. After a rename the window, and `tine page rename` (new `report.site_exceptions`), list every place that could not take the new name and every property key rewritten in key spelling. Favorites and the home page follow every name under the renamed page, including names that only a link or the settings hold; after a merge, Favorites list each page once in its first place (favorites `A, X, B` with "merge A into B" give `B, X`), while a plain rename no longer drops a repeated entry; and config.edn is updated all at once or not at all, with the window saying when it was not. A property key under the renamed page (`a/y::` when renaming `A` to `B`) now follows like a link to the same page, even when `A/y` exists only by reference, and the label of a Markdown file link (`[Old](file:x.md)`, `[Old](../pages/x.md)`, and an image link such as `![Old](file:x.md)` that names the page) takes the new name, as an Org file link's label does. A formatted label (`[**Old**](file:x.md)`) keeps its formatting; one whose formatting splits the name (`[**Ol**_d_](…)`) is left and listed. A new name holding Markdown syntax (`a]b`, a backslash as in `New\\Tail`) is written escaped, so the label names exactly the new page; a label that no spelling would make name it is left and listed. A rename that changes no page file (every place naming the page cannot take the new name) still counts as a rename: Favorites and the home page follow it, and `tine page rename` answers `renamed`. A day the rename newly produces that several journal files claim is refused as contested, naming every file (REG-CM-S2-MD-FILE-LABEL, REG-CM-S2-FORMATTED-LABEL, REG-CM-S2-TOUCHED-CAPTURE, REG-CM-S2-TOUCHED-CONTESTED, REG-CM-S2-DAY-IMAGE-CONTESTED, REG-CM-S2-SITE-REPORT, REG-CM-S2-SETTINGS, REG-CM-S2-SETTINGS-NO-BYTES, REG-CM-S2-KEY-PREFIX).

items.text: **Changed:** renaming follows the conceptual model's request rules. A name that is no page and no alias, and a journal day, are refused with a reason. Days are never respelled by a rename: renaming `ns` keeps `[[ns/2026-10-26]]` pointing at its journal, and the old journal-reference refusal is gone. Renaming a page to another page's alias is refused, naming the page that alias opens (no more merge or "make it its own page" choice there); renaming a page to its own alias is one step and keeps the declaration. A moved file with conflict markers that would need changes is refused instead of moving with a stale title. `tine page rename` renames an alias itself, not the page declaring it, renames to a page's own alias, and reports planner refusals as `refused` (`page-exists` or the new `rename-refused`) with `admitted: false` instead of `uncertain`, including a day typed as `2026-10-26` under a title format without a year. The rules hold for a request naming the page's own name too, and property keys and query arguments spelled as a day keep their spelling. With a journal title format without a year (such as `MM-dd`), renaming or merging onto a full date like `2026-10-26`, and opening it by name, now reach only that day's journal instead of every journal sharing its label (clicking a `[[2026-10-26]]` link still goes by the label). (REG-CM-S1-NOT-A-PAGE, REG-CM-S1-DAY-SOURCE, REG-CM-S1-DAY-LABEL, REG-CM-S1-DAY-PINNED, REG-CM-S1-ALIAS-HELD, REG-CM-S1-OWN-ALIAS, REG-CM-S1-MARKED-MOVE, REG-CM-S1-CLI-ALIAS, REG-CM-S1-KEY-DAY, REG-CM-S1-SAME-NAME, REG-CM-S1-CLI-TYPED-DAY).

items.text: **Changed:** a page merge writes what the conceptual model's merge rule says. The aliases of both pages become one alias property holding each name once, names compared as Tine reads which page they open: `C\#` and `C#`, `ML` and `ml`, or two spellings of one day keep only the first spelling, and the spelling left over is no longer kept in a block. The page that remains keeps its own header; a source property joins it when the remaining page does not have that key (`foo_bar` and `foo-bar` are one key; when a rename merges the pages, keys are compared after the rename, so `old::` meets `new::`, and the source's title left in the merge block names the new page). The block between the two bodies appears only when the source header leaves lines there (a title, a clashing or repeated property, other text), never for blank lines or alias syntax. A merge stops, changing no files, when an Org source drawer entry clashes with one the remaining page has, since inside the quote it would lose its references, when blocks under the source header would have no leftover block to hang under, or when the remaining page's own header would give it another title (REG-CM-MW-ALIAS-READING, REG-CM-MW-LEFTOVER, REG-CM-MW-RENAME-MAP).

items.text: The updater is configured to install an update only when its signature names the version the update server offers, so a compromised server cannot get an older, genuinely signed Tine installed as a newer one: such an update may still be listed as available, and installing it is refused. The release check refuses a signature whose trusted comment line does not name the release version. The app's own verifier is the authority, and it also refuses signatures this check cannot judge, such as wrapped or malformed ones (#983).
